bullets.title: NVDA Earnings: Beat + 70% FY28 Revenue Guidance, Sell-the-News Repeating
bullets.body: Nvidia posted record Q2 revenue of $96.2B (+106% YoY), beating $92.3B consensus, with data center revenue of $89B (+117% YoY). CFO guided Q3 at $108B (+2%) and guided FY28 revenue growth to ~70% supply-constrained—well above prior consensus of ~45%. Despite the massive beat, shares initially sold off, repeating a pattern seen in four of the last six quarters. Relief rally quickly followed as multiple sell-side raised PTs (Raymond James to $515, JPMorgan to $320, Bernstein to $400).

bullets.title: Warsh Jackson Hole Speech Hawkish: September Rate Hike Odds Jump to ~56%
bullets.body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation is 'more concerning,' characterized financial conditions as 'hard-pressed to describe as restrictive,' and signaled more work is needed if inflation doesn't move toward 2% 'with speed.' September hike odds jumped from ~33% the prior day to 56% per Polymarket, and short-term rate futures fell sharply. Chicago PMI also crushed at 47.1 vs. 57.9 expected.

bullets.title: Goolsbee at Jackson Hole: Inflation Is Primary Concern, But Patient
bullets.body: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee expressed growing concern about economic overheating while saying he is 'not losing patience on inflation.' He flagged demand-driven inflation as difficult to fix and indicated he's willing to wait for data before further action. Hammack separately called for immediate rate hikes, saying the economy is unrestricted.

bullets.title: S&P Market Cap: NVDA + MSFT Drove Virtually All Tech Gains This Earnings Season
bullets.body: The S&P gained $1.75T in market cap this earnings season, with tech accounting for $1.39T. Of that, NVDA and MSFT combined for $1.415T—the other 71 tech constituents saw a combined $22B decline. The top 22 S&P stocks now have a larger combined market cap ($35.5T) than the bottom 478 combined ($35T).

bullets.title: META $18B Settlement with State AGs Over Youth Harm; $10B Q3 Charge
bullets.body: Meta agreed to pay up to $18B over 10 years to settle claims from US states that its platforms harmed children and improperly collected youth data. The company will accrue ~$10B in legal expenses in Q3. Investors treated the outcome positively—shares rallied 4%+ at one point as it removes the existential risk of a verdict that could have approached $1.4T.

bullets.title: Salesforce ClaudeForce Launch + 22% Earnings Rally
bullets.body: Salesforce announced 'ClaudeForce' in partnership with Anthropic, embedding Claude directly into the Salesforce platform with a Sept 2026 beta. CRM surged 22% on earnings (Q2 revenue $11.35B beat, raised FY guidance). The move was described as positioning CRM vs. Palantir's open-weight strategy.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Financing: Blue Owl $2.4B Nvidia Chip Deal; Lambda $1B; Anthropic $45B Nscale
bullets.body: Multiple large private-market AI infrastructure deals were flagged: Blue Owl led a $2.4B debt deal to purchase Nvidia chips; Lambda secured ~$1B in private short-term debt (proceeds financing NVDA GPUs for Microsoft leasing); Anthropic committed $45B to Nscale Compute for 460MW of Vera Rubin capacity over six years. NVDA itself entered MOUs to mobilize $500B+ in third-party capital.

bullets.title: DRAM Prices Surge to Gold Equivalent; SK Hynix CEO Sees Shortage Through 2030
bullets.body: A kilogram of Korean DRAM chips now costs the equivalent of 620 grams of gold, up from a 2023 trough of 120 grams. SK Hynix CEO dismissed oversupply risk and sees a memory chip crunch through end of 2030. Chinese rival CXMT reported 873% YoY revenue growth in H1 2026, claiming the No. 4 global DRAM position.

bullets.title: MRVL Earnings: Beat but 'Sell-the-News' on Margin Trajectory; CXL Momentum
bullets.body: Marvell Q2 FY2027 beat estimates ($2.74B revenue, +37% YoY; $0.94 adj EPS) and guided Q3 to $3.15B (+15% QoQ), raising FY27 to ~$12B. Stock sold off 7-8% AH on high expectations and slightly below-consensus margin guidance. Author at Hot Chips saw meaningful CXL ecosystem momentum building with more news expected by year-end.

bullets.title: Marvell Switch-Silicon Gaining vs. Broadcom; Validates Arista Demand
bullets.body: MRVL's traction in switch-silicon identified as a share risk to AVGO while simultaneously validating Arista's demand outlook. Optical interconnect and Ethernet gaining share in AI infrastructure spending per MRVL's Q2 call.

bullets.title: Yen Breaks 160/USD; Japan FX Intervention Hits Record 15.4T Yen
bullets.body: USD/JPY broke 160 for the first time since July 31. Japan conducted a record $98.7B in FX intervention over the prior month. Bessent defended the intervention to Senator Warren, clarifying no credit was extended to Japan and Japan owes the Treasury nothing. 30-year Treasury yield near 5.21% while 5-year hit 4.48%, its highest since February.

bullets.title: NVDA Acquires Hugging Face for $12.9B; SpaceX Partnership for Space-Optimized Vera Rubin
bullets.body: Multiple credible outlets reported Nvidia agreed to acquire open-source AI model platform Hugging Face for $12.9B. Separately, Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX and Nvidia designed a space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 system planned for orbit in Q4, scaling significantly in 2028.

bullets.title: OpenAI Jalapeño ASIC Claims 2x Better Perf/W vs. NVDA Blackwell; AVGO as Partner
bullets.body: OpenAI unveiled Jalapeño at Hot Chips, claiming up to 1.5-1.9x better throughput/watt vs. Nvidia GB200/GB300 and 1.7-3.6x lower latency, at 700W vs. Nvidia's 1,200-1,400W. AVGO and CLS confirmed as partners. Authors note Jalapeño is at B0 stage, with production ramp likely 2027-2028—not an immediate threat to Nvidia's installed base.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Rubin HBM Content Downgrade Alert; 192GB 8-Hi vs. Prior 1TB Spec
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis reported Nvidia Rubin Ultra will ship with only 192GB of HBM4 8-hi—characterized as a massive downgrade from the original preview of 1TB HBM and now below standard Rubin's 288GB. Implications for HBM suppliers are mixed.

bullets.title: AMD Upgrades + Strong Server CPU Share; Intel 18A Yields Ahead of Schedule
bullets.body: Raymond James upgraded AMD to Strong Buy with $641 PT on server CPU market growth to $201B by 2030 (44% 5Y CAGR). AMD's x86 market share crossed 30% for the first time (server segment at 46.4%); Intel 18A-P is tracking yields ahead of target per DB conference. INTC gained 2.37% on the Intel news.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Sector Volatility Reset; Bull Flag Building
bullets.body: Semiconductor volatility saw one of its largest resets in years following the week's events. Options flow showed large call activity (NVDA $50M+, SPY $1.1B call wall at 770) supporting upside. The broader tech vs. semis basket hit 4-month highs and was up 70% from June lows.

bullets.title: IREN Reports: Revenue Beat, Massive Net Loss From Mining Hardware Write-Off
bullets.body: Iris Energy reported Q4 revenue of $137M (beat $135M est.) but a net loss of $684M, including $450M in non-cash impairments as mining hardware was decommissioned for AI conversion. Stock fell 10%+. Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $19.2M from $59.5M prior quarter on higher capex spend.

bullets.title: Nancy Pelosi Discloses Up to $12M in Bloom Energy + Intel Calls
bullets.body: Pelosi disclosed purchasing 15,000 shares of Bloom Energy (BE) plus call options worth up to $12M expiring June 2027, plus 10,000 INTC shares and calls. BE surged 10-12% following the disclosure as copytraders piled in.

bullets.title: Bessent 'Operation Economic Outcast' Targets Iran; Major Bank Sanctions This Week
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent launched 'Operation Economic Outcast,' sanctioning 60+ Iran-linked entities and targeting five key sectors (digital assets, tech, gold, aviation, shipping). Bessent warned a major financial institution will be sanctioned by week's end and that any country facilitating Iran dealings faces removal from the dollar system. Iran's rial hit a record low of 2.027M/USD.

bullets.title: Alibaba $10B Share Sale for AI; Jack Ma Buys $76.5M; Qwen Downloads #1 Globally
bullets.body: Alibaba raised HK$80B (~$10B) to fund AI; shares rose 3%+ in Hong Kong. Separately, co-founders Jack Ma and Eddie Wu bought $25.7M in BABA shares. Alibaba's open-weight Qwen models surpassed Meta and Google to rank No. 1 globally by downloads at 3B+ in six months.
